questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Getting closer to nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Super nice place for an exchange semester. The reason I don't rate it higher is the academic program and the courses which where not the best for me.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Good if you attend the welcome days at the uni.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Help with setting up my courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I would definitely reccoment checking out
hybel.no
. I made a profile and got many offers - one of which I said yes to. I have been living with three amazing norwegian girls in a cool place.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You are not gonna be a part of the Erasmus bubble out at Fantoft, where most international students live, but I preferred it to be more of an authentic experience. If you want the international community and events set up for you go for Fantoft Sammen accomodation. I found it easy to make friends through climbing, BSI events, and school so that was enough for me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you're into it I think fantoft can be good. It was my impression that basically all students that applied for the campus housing ended up there so don't bother spending time looking at the other SAMMEN places and ranking your priorities when applying. You'll most likely get Fantoft anyway.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was okay - however, a bit slow on their part.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to apply for the uni itself and then courses were preapproved ish. However, they couldn't tell me which courses I actually got into until a week or two before classes started so it felt a little chaotic.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I went to the student counselling at the Faculty of Mathematics and Natural sciences and got some help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Eventually I got the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check if you match the criteria for the course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was alright. New insights, but some of the cool courses were not open to exchange students so even though im more into marine biology I ended up having a lot of courses related to fisheries directly more so than ecology and the biology of organisms.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The MA courses were sufficiently challenging but the BA courses were very easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Two of three courses were similar to DK with lectures and assignments. One course was group learning based. Not for me.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
SDG214 Sustainable Development Goal 14: Life below water
BIO356 Stock Monitoring and Responsible Harvesting
BIO339 Ecosystem and Fisheries Assessment Models

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would probably say BIO356 because we went out with the G.O. sars research vessel of the Institute of Marine Research which was very cool and I learned a lot. However, the course is very specific to the use of hydro accoustics and the use of ecchosounders so relatively niche. The part of the course that focused on responsible harvest was super cool and interesting.

questions.answer: It was as expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Lots of opportunities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Heaps. I would reccoment checking out BSI friluft. I got my belaying certificate there in the beginning of the semester on Tuesday-climbing. And SAMMEN has a cheap membership for the semester which allows you to use all of their fitness-gyms and swimming-pool and stuff like that.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: BSI friluft - nice trips.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Rent a car and go to Hoddevika to go surfing. was so nice. 
And you can rent gear for free at BUA. Super handy.
And! go alpine skiing in Voss and Myrkdalen.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very similar to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Live with them. 
And learn some norwegian. It really pays off.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The Norwegians' appreciation for nature and getting out.
Ut på tur, aldrig sur.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Get out in the mountains around bergen - bring your outdoor gear. 
Go to some of the cute saunas around town - for instance Laugaren. 
If you're into climbing then you NEED to check out Vestveggen . It's a huge rope climbing gym right outside town and of course outdoor climbing in the area.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Don't let the rain scare you. I was concerned before coming here but it was truly not that bad. And when the weather is nice there are a million things to do in this city and the mountains around it. 
The most amazing DNT hut I've ever been to called Stovegolvet is also definitely worth a mention and a visit.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Nature!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to plan my masters thesis at home at the same time as being here.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Bergen is a super cute place to go if you're into mountains, skiing, hiking, climbing - all that jazz. Stay curious of new places during your entire stay and you'll get some amazing experiences.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
